messages.subject: Average temporal trend
parts:
I have built a spatio-temporal SPDE model following this tutorial (https://www.paulamoraga.com/book-geospatial/sec-geostatisticaldataexamplest.html). My model is producing reasonable local-scale counts at different time/space combinations, but I also need to know the general temporal trend in the count i.e. the average counts in each year across the entire field/extent (e.g. Spain).

Is it as simple as adding f(time, model = "rw2), or do I need to acknowledge the grouped nature of the time-series? 

Can anyone advise?

Tom Johnson
University of Sheffield

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Average temporal trend
parts:
Hi Tom Johnson,

If your linear predictor is
intercept + beta * covariate + spatio.temporal
as you mentioned, the spatio-temporal model term could capture the
temporal overall trend, but it needs to be summarized integrating over
space for each time.

However, you may want to add a term in the linear predictor to capture
it, particularly if there is an overall common trend. If you then have
intercept + beta * covariate + temporal + spatio.temporal
then the temporal term will capture it.

Best regards,
Elias
